text: In March 2014, twenty-five of us said "the president's budget," first among us P000601. Then twenty-two of us said "comprehensive immigration reform." On the same late-March day, twenty of us reached for "a discharge petition" — John B. Larson said it first, back in 2013 — and fifteen of us moved together to "force a vote." Fifteen of us named the bill three ways in the same breath: "border security economic opportunity and immigration," "security economic opportunity and immigration modernization," "economic opportunity and immigration modernization act." Fifteen of us said "on h r." We converged on March 26: the petition, the vote, the bill's long name, repeated across us on one day. We record it as it happened. The budget came first and widest; the immigration mechanism came later and narrower, and we said it in near-unison.
